nodes.summary: A map `g` into `Convexity.StdSimplex ℝ X` (`X` finite) is continuous as soon as every weight `t ↦ (g t).weights x` is continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity criterion for maps into a simplex

nodes.summary: Each weight `∏ᵢ σᵢ(sᵢ)` is a product of coordinate functions, continuous on the product of simplices.
nodes.title: The product distribution depends continuously on its factors

nodes.summary: Every continuous self-map of `Convexity.StdSimplex ℝ X`, for a finite nonempty type `X`, has a fixed point. Transported from `exists_fixedPoint` along an enumeration `X ≃ Fin (n + 1)`.
nodes.title: Brouwer's fixed-point theorem for simplices with any finite vertex set

nodes.summary: Every continuous self-map of a finite product `∏ᵢ Δ(Sᵢ)` of simplices with nonempty finite vertex sets has a fixed point. The product is a retract of the simplex `Δ(∏ᵢ Sᵢ)` (product distribution, then marginals), so the statement follows from `exists_fixedPoint_of_finite`. This is the form of Brouwer's theorem used in J. Nash, "Non-cooperative games", Ann. of Math. 54 (1951), 286–295, where the product of the…
nodes.title: Brouwer's fixed-point theorem for products of simplices

nodes.summary: Every continuous map `f` of the standard simplex `Δⁿ = Convexity.StdSimplex ℝ (Fin (n + 1))` to itself has a fixed point.
nodes.title: Brouwer's fixed-point theorem for the standard simplex

nodes.summary: A continuous self-map of the standard simplex has a point `x` with `Function.IsFixedPt f x`; a restatement of `exists_fixedPoint` in Mathlib's fixed-point vocabulary.
nodes.title: Brouwer's theorem for the simplex, fixed-point form

nodes.summary: For every map `f` of the standard simplex to itself and every point `x`, some coordinate `i` in the support of `x` has `f(x)ᵢ ≤ xᵢ`: otherwise summing `xᵢ < f(x)ᵢ` over the support would give `1 < ∑ᵢ f(x)ᵢ = 1`.
nodes.title: The Brouwer sets satisfy the KKM covering condition

nodes.summary: For a map `g` between finite types, the pushforward `p.map g` of a distribution `p` gives `y` the total weight `∑_{g x = y} p(x)` of its preimage; in particular the `i`-th marginal of a distribution on `∀ i, S i` is `p.map (fun s => s i)`.
nodes.title: Weights of a pushforward distribution

nodes.summary: The `i`-th marginal `(prodSimplex σ).map (fun s => s i)` of the product of independent distributions `σⱼ` is `σᵢ`: summing `∏ⱼ σⱼ(sⱼ)` over the profiles with `sᵢ = t` leaves `σᵢ(t)`, since every other factor sums to `1`.
nodes.title: The marginals of a product distribution are its factors

nodes.summary: A nonnegative function `w` on a finite type with `∑ₓ w x = 1`, packaged as a point of `Convexity.StdSimplex ℝ X`.
nodes.title: Probability vector from a function

nodes.summary: The product distribution `s ↦ ∏ᵢ σᵢ(sᵢ)` on `∀ i, S i` of independent distributions `σᵢ` on the finite sets `S i` (in game theory, the distribution of pure profiles under independent mixed strategies).
nodes.title: Product distribution

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
